findings.breaking_input: Any caller of find() that still passes two arguments (find(ctx, name)), such as a teardown, plan or other verify path in this file that the diff does not show. orgId is then undefined, not null.
findings.why: The unscoped branch tests `=== null`, so undefined falls through. Any same-named project then either throws PROJECT_UNSCOPED or, once organization_id is present, is filtered against undefined and dropped. A teardown or plan that relied on find would then see no project and report absent, or throw a coded refusal out of a read. Only scaffold and probe were updated in the diff, so the unchanged callers are unchecked. This is the pattern 'an answer read as absent' plus 'every catch fix: list every code the guarded body can throw'.
findings.fix: Give the parameter a default (`orgId = null`) or use `orgId == null`. Grep the file for every find( call. Add a fixture for each caller, with and without a named org.
findings.twin_of: An order list answered without `items` was read as "no order", so a second order would be created -> every check-then-create: is an unreadable answer ever read as absent?

findings.where: products/launch/providers/database/supabase.mjs:scaffold (`const orgId = named(ctx) === null ? null : await org(ctx)`) and find unscoped branch
findings.breaking_input: No supabase_org is set, the token sees 2 orgs, and one same-named project already exists in either org (the owner's own `arc-sandbox` in the first org).
findings.why: When unnamed, org() is skipped before find, and find returns every same-named project across the whole account. scaffold adopts it as `supabase-project-found` and never reaches the ORG_AMBIGUOUS refusal. ADR-1773 says launch never picks between orgs, but here the project's org is the pick, and the probe then writes launch_probe into whichever org's project matched. The same happens in probe(), so verify passes against it. This is the 'existence checked on one target set, the write covered another' pattern.
findings.fix: Always resolve org(ctx) first, even when unnamed, so several orgs without a name refuse before any lookup. Then scope find to that id in every case.
findings.twin_of: Existence checked on one target set, the write covered another -> every check-then-create: does the create's scope equal the check's?

findings.where: products/launch/providers/database/supabase.mjs:org and seen (o.id / o.name on list elements)
findings.breaking_input: GET /organizations answers an array containing a null or non-object element, for example [null, {"id":"o2","name":"acme"}], with supabase_org: acme.
findings.why: `orgs.filter((o) => o.id === want ...)` and seen() dereference each element, so a null throws a raw TypeError. That is an uncoded error, so verify's coded-refusal catch does not turn it into an answer, and it escapes as a throw. The same pattern was already fixed for `errors || []`, where the provider was trusted to send objects.
findings.fix: Drop or refuse non-object elements before filtering, for example `orgs.filter((o) => o && typeof o === "object")`, and refuse if any were dropped.
findings.twin_of: `errors || []` trusted the provider to send an array of objects -> every `x || []` over a response body
